### problem_chain

**Root — pass the cover to the new owner with the piece.** The customer asks only this: "*what he
wants from the protection desk is that the cover on it should go with the piece instead of stopping
when he hands it over*". The policy whose own rule describes that result is
`protection_ext_transfer_carryover` (`trigger: on_request`, `subject: [protection_plan_transferred]`,
`computes: allowance_carried_across`, `target_tool: confirm_coverage_transfer_42b50f64`,
`owner="user"`).

**Its rule carries exactly two prerequisite sentences:**
> "What carries across to the new owner is fixed only after the allowance entries booked to the plan carry a grant for the coverage year in progress."
> "Coverage passes to a new owner only once every claim entered against the plan that the coverage does not answer for carries the ground on which it was refused."

**Edge A — is the first state true at `frozen_time`? No.** `effective_date` is `2022-03-14`, so the
coverage year in progress opened on the anniversary `2026-03-14` (`MONTHS(2022-03-14, 2026-09-17) =
54`, `54 % 12 = 6` whole months into it). The allowance entries on the plan are:

| entry | date | amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fc74c757…` `protection_allowance_granted` | 2022-03-14 | +5 000.00 |
| `00c2be8f…` `protection_allowance_reinstated` | 2023-03-14 | +5 000.00 |
| `08773606…` `protection_allowance_reinstated` | 2024-03-14 | +5 000.00 |
| `c5fefa26…` `protection_allowance_reinstated` | 2025-03-14 | +5 000.00 |

The 2026-03-14 grant was never booked; the most recent stands 18 whole months back. **No allowance
entry falls inside the coverage year in progress**, so the edge's condition is genuinely unmet.

**Edge B — is the second state true? No.** The claims entered against the plan:

| claim reference | filed | answered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CL-321102` | 2024-11-05 +900.00 `chain_break` | settled `dbf1c986…` 2024-11-19 −640.00 |
| `CL-321503` | 2025-07-30 +3 400.00 `stone_loss` | settled `dcf8d8cb…` 2025-08-10 −3 150.00 |
| `CL-321640` | 2026-01-08 +1 200.00 `clasp_replacement` | settled `93784231…` 2026-01-20 −900.00 |
| `CL-321884` | 2026-05-06 +12 900.00 `chain_break` | **nothing** |

`CL-321884` is one the coverage does **not** answer for, and it carries no ground. Why the coverage
does not answer for it, derived from the records and the inherited base policy alone:
`inspection_interval_months = 6` and the inspection before the loss is
`protection_ledger[ebf84938…] 2025-09-12`, so the next was due 2026-03-12; `inspection_grace_days =
45` carries good standing only to 2026-04-26; `missed_inspection_suspends_coverage = true`. The loss
was entered 2026-05-06 and the piece taken in 2026-05-07 — inside the spell out of good standing.
`protection_inspection_discipline` then settles it: "*An inspection logged inside the restoration
window puts the lapse right and coverage resumes from the day the inspection was logged, never
retrospectively, so a loss that happened while the coverage was out of good standing stays refused.*"
The restoring inspection is 2026-06-08, after the loss. So the single ground is the inspection lapse
(`denial_reason_code = inspection_lapse`, `claim_outcome = denied_inspection_lapse`), and **not** an
excluded peril: `chain_break` is in the Care Plan 5-Year's `covered_perils`. **The edge's condition is
genuinely unmet.**

**Which writes bring those states about?** Following each sentence with no tool name in it:
`reinstate_benefit_allowance_e0b143ff` for edge A and `record_claim_refusal_9dff8781` for edge B. See
`_difficulty.md` → `### prerequisite_sentences` (**E2**, **E3**) for the demonstration that exactly one
write of this difficulty produces each state and that each sentence admits one reading.

**Do either of those problems carry prerequisites of their own?** No.
`protection_ext_allowance_reinstatement.rule` and `protection_ext_claim_refusal.rule` contain no
sentence joining their own result to a state they wait on with an ordering connective (the "one after
another and each on the figure the one before it left" in the former orders steps inside its own
arithmetic). Their inherited eligibility already holds: `grantable_state` allows `active`
(`status = active`); the claim stands open with no answer against its reference. The walk terminates.

```
protection_ext_transfer_carryover           (root, owner=user, on_request)
   ├─ value_input, gate=granted_in_window ──► protection_ext_allowance_reinstatement  (owner=agent, state_due)
   └─ value_input, gate=claims_share      ──► protection_ext_claim_refusal            (owner=agent, state_due)
```

- nodes: 3; prerequisite problems: n = 2 (within 1–3)
- `value_input` edges: 2, against a floor of max(n − 1, 1) = 1 ✓
- no cycle
- topological order: {reinstatement, refusal} → transfer

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip one prerequisite write, replay everything else unchanged,
recompute the root:

Both edges bear weight, and each moves a **value**, not a status flip — which is why both are
`value_input` and why their gates (`granted_in_window`, `claims_share`) are the bindings they
actually move.

**Parallel edges and the terminal state.** The root has two out-edges, so the order between the two
prerequisite writes had to be pinned down rather than assumed. The refusal's
`services_window_months` does read allowance entries, so the two orders were **recomputed**:

| order | `grants_this_year` at the refusal | `services_window_months` | `chain_repairs_drawn` | `refusals_in_window` | `refused_amount` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reinstatement → refusal | 1 | 6 | 0 | 0 | **10 061.00** |
| refusal → reinstatement | 0 | 12 | 0 | 0 | **10 061.00** |

Both windows contain zero chain-break settlements (the only one is 22 months back) and zero refusals,
so both tiers of both ladders resolve identically and **one terminal state** follows on either order.

compute` reads `protection_allowance_reinstated`, `protection_claim_settled`,

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now, three writes.** Nothing waits (check 5). The transfer is not refused:
Care Plan 5-Year carries `transfer_allowed: true`, the plan stands `active`, and the inspection the
coverage requires is already logged. The claim is refused — that is itself one of the three writes,
on the single ground the records fix.

**User need, authorisation and timing.**
- *object* — "*a platinum riviere necklace he bought his late wife in 2022*"; exactly one
  `protection_plans` row exists (`7788a58b…`, `covered_item_sku NECK-32860`,
  `purchased_date 2022-03-14`).
- *timing* — "*he wants it arranged today, because she collects it at the weekend*". Act at
  `frozen_time`.
- *authorisation boundary* — "*He is content for the desk to do whatever the record needs on his
  side, but says he understands he has to be the one to sign the piece over himself, and he will do
  that while he is on the line.*" This maps exactly onto the owners: the reinstatement and the
  refusal are `owner="agent"`, the transfer is `owner="user"` and is handed over.
- *terminal state* — the cover stands in the daughter's name. `new_owner_name` is fixed verbatim:
  "*Delphine Thibodeaux-Moreau, and he is particular that it be written exactly that way, hyphen and
  all*", which is precisely what the tool's Verbatim-class argument demands ("*copied character for
  character, keeping their wording, spelling and punctuation exactly*").

**The root problem only.** The customer names neither prerequisite. "*He raises nothing else about
the plan; as far as he is concerned it has been quiet.*" The repair, the payment at the counter and
the lapsed check-up surface only "*Only when he is asked*". His two conditional reactions — "*If the
agent tells him the claim from the spring is being refused…*", "*If the agent tells him the benefit
for this year has been put back on the plan…*" — fire only after the agent has reached the
conclusion. He issues no second item of work. He closes where the writes close: "*once he hears that
the cover stands in his daughter's name he thanks the agent … and rings off with nothing further to
ask*". One line is recorded as an observation below (**W-1**) because, once the agent has announced
the refusal, it supplies the ground.

the difficulty of one scored argument for an agent that announces a refusal before working out why.

actually paid at the counter. The seeded amount is what puts the customer on tier 2 of
`recorded_figure_basis` rather than its fall-through, so it is load-bearing; the tiers' own conditions
and outcomes (cap the recorded figure at the value the piece is taken at) are ones the line of
business does hold. Recorded as an observation about the seeded input, not about a ladder.
